title: BSD MITM contract

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: The tracer historically labels this field assigned_pid.

workflows.purpose: Observe a BSD client without changing its lifecycle.

steps.action: Forward every call, handle, PID descriptor, clone, and close unchanged.
steps.notes: Do not synthesize RegisterClient or StartMonitoring.

workflows.purpose: Model the common libnx BSD client shape.

sessions.description: Root session that owns RegisterClient and socket traffic.
Separate short root session used for StartMonitoring.
Additional data sessions cloned from the data root when configured.

steps.action: Open a separate BSD root service.
Register the client with its transfer memory and original PID semantics.
Start monitoring with the returned client identifier.
Clone the data root only when more BSD sessions are configured.
Close clones before their owning sessions and preserve the observed teardown order.

workflows.notes: Two root sessions are common observed libnx behavior, not a proven universal BSD requirement.

workflows.purpose: Isolate the first lifecycle phase that prevents a clean relaunch.

steps.action: Open one root session, create transfer memory, and call RegisterClient.
Close the visible session and transfer memory, then repeat the same launch.
Only after a stable baseline, add a separate monitor session and StartMonitoring.
Only after monitoring is stable, add root clones.
Only after lifecycle phases are stable, add sockets and traffic.

constraints: BSD descriptors belong to the client/session created by RegisterClient.
Preserve original PID forwarding semantics for RegisterClient.
A passive MITM must treat monitor sessions and root clones as independently owned objects.
Do not infer bsd:u, bsd:s, or bsd:a from packets alone.

provenance.reference: controlled BSD client traces on firmware 20.5.0
